title: Trap by Shamalamadingdong and all the plot holes or terrible writing

commenti.body:
> Shamalamadingdong

It took more effort to type this than it did to spell his name properly. I've never understood the urge to do this to his name at all, and I never see people do this with the names of white directors.

To your post: Yeah, the film is terrible, probably his worst after *Old*, and it's entirely a vehicle for his daughter's music career. None of it makes sense in any way shape or form.

> I’ve never understood the urge to do this to his name at all

“Foreign names are weird unlike mine, therefore it’s funny to mock them by messing up their names on purpose”
[removed]

First of all, your title is disrespectful. Shyamalan is a veteran writer and director, and deserves more than your juvenile response, regardless of what you think of the film. Also, I hope you understand that by directly criticizing his writing, you open yourself up to similar criticism. For instance, rather than sharing any sort of fully-formed thoughts and opinions, you share knee-jerk responses and questions. Why should you expect us to answer questions that you should first consider for yourself. It makes you sound intellectually undeveloped.

Agreed.


Don't get how the writers could create something with so many plot holes.


Yea I put effort into Shamalamadingdong, or I my phone auto completes. Must have put effort into getting mad about the joke.

Movie had so much potential and the plot wholes ruin it. That being said I was still able to enjoy it. John Harnet carries the film. Just gotta turn ypur brain way off and enjoy what did work. No where near his worse

Lol


Imagine getting personally offended at a funny name for famous people

Naga-naga-not gonna work here anymore. 

It is just dumb jokes. A trope. Lazy.

Loved the movie. Don’t care about that type of stuff. If you needlessly pick at every plot yea things maybe won’t make sense. The entire premise was probably extremely illegal anyways. Some stop and frisk esque shit. But it’s a thriller dude fucking rear window was also ridiculous if you start to think about it purely through the lens of “WELL THATS JUST NOT REALISTIC AND MAKES NO SENSE”
Yea I mean it was fun. I was curious with the happenings by mind blown by the writing.

I don't think it's a terrible film. It has, at times, an interesting vibe, as well as decent thematic development and good performances. It's clear thought went into it. Which is more than I can say for genuinely terrible films. But it does feel rushed out, as if Shyamalan put his first draft onto paper, or perhaps into chatgpt, and just sailed into production with that. I suppose when you're wealthy and largely fund your own projects, you can do that. But it did need revision at the writing stage, because it created problems that the editing stage couldn't really solve. Overall I don't regret watching it though. And I think it's a great idea for a father to support his daughters' careers like this—both of his daughters seem to have some talent, and as a dad myself, I know I'd put the effort in like this if I had his resources.

first of all the movie is subjectively great, fun, and campy. going to a shyamalan movie for an intellectual thriller is ur problem. second of all spell the mans name right and dont disrespect other cultures especially when criticizing someones work. fucking asshole
I'm not mad, I'm pointing out that the "joke" isn't actually funny.
also i didnt read ur whole post cuz u deserve no attention
Then don't laugh.

Shyamalan has been plagued by it his entire career, and it's always come across being - at the very least - xenophobic to me. No part for it in any decent or objective analysis

I'm not going to pretend like Trap or Old are objectively good films but there's no way they can be the worst in a filmography that includes After Earth and The Last Airbender, let alone The Happening or Lady In The Water
Shamalamadingdong

Honestly I have huge respect for him just saying, "yeah, I want to help launch your career, let's make a 90 minute music video". Personally I didn't enjoy the film at all but I *have* listened to Saleka's music off the back of it, so to that end it's a complete success.
go stare at the sun huberman boy

I had genuinely completely forgotten about The Last Air bender, and admittedly haven't seen After Earth and didn't realise he directed it. I definitely think The Happening and Lady In The Water are better than Old and Trap but it's not a hill I'm willing to die on.
Shamalamadingdong?
Thank you so much for saying this.  I agree completely that the movie is absolute garbage but I could not read the post, I could not get past the title because of the name thing.

> Shyamalan is a veteran writer and director, and deserves more than your juvenile response, regardless of what you think of the film.

I can't even imagine saying this about the self-aggrandizing dingus who's responsible for *The Lady in the Water*.

I'd love to live in a world where I'd forgotten The Last Airbender. I have no experience of the original source material, I can't imagine how much I'd have hated the film if I had love for that to start with

The Happening probably is better to be fair, I'm going to rewatch it soon and expect to like it more. I thought Old and Trap were at least fun, whereas LITW just utterly bored me

It is funny that people still go in relatively decent numbers to watch every new film he puts out, and then complain about the same issues every film since maybe Signs or The Village has had
I don't know what your name is, but either way, you kind of seem like a dickhead.

Yeah it's very strange, I'm definitely one of the people who keeps giving him chances despite really knowing I should know better by now. I think it's because he's proven that when he's good he does make really great films that don't really feel like anyone else. *Unbreakable* and *The Sixth Sense* are fantastic and I'll defend *The Village* until my last breath. And even when they're bad they're still mostly in that "so bad it's good" territory (at least for me, I know a lot of people don't feel that way about *Lady In The Water* specifically). *Old* and *Trap* don't even have the decency to be so bad they're good, though. 

After *Trap* I told myself I won't give him any more chances but part of me knows that I'll watch his next film whatever happens, and I'm not sure why I extend that grace to him over other directors who I've decided not to bother with any more.

I think it's because, for better or worse, there's nobody else that is really doing what he does. You can't watch one of his post-The Visit films are mistake it or for anyone else. In a world of remakes, franchises and identikit Blumhouse horror, you know that a new Shyamalan film is going to be something he wants to make, and he'll get performances out of actors that nobody else possibly could (or would likely even try to).

Trap may be a vehicle for his daughter's singing career, it may have moments where logic go completely out of the window, and parts that feel like pure parody - but I went to see it in the cinema (albeit unexpectedly, I walked out of Longlegs because it was full of obnoxious teens and saw Trap on whim instead) and enjoyed it more than objectively better films I've seen this year. I can't be mad at that.

I rewatched Signs recently, highly enjoyed it. Old was cool too.


I just think Trap went overboard with the terrible inconsistency and errors in writing.

Yeah I think you're right about that. He's got a very singular voice, even when it's speaking nonsense, and there's a lot to like about that.

I do wonder if I would have liked Trap more had I seen it in the cinema. I bet it plays great as a festival film.

I'll definitely watch his films no doubt. I like most of his work.


Just amazed at the amount of bad writing in Trap.

"veteran" just means he's been doing this for awhile. even if i don't like one or two or more of his films, or even most of them, i respect the individual and the effort. that's an essential part of what it means to be a fully socialized human being.
